rules.interpretation: When a ship is stolen, attached Effects stay attached and retain their existing ownership. Vehicles/starships carried aboard and their weapons/devices are stolen. Native must retain the official Effect rule despite pinned GEMP divergence.

sourceFindings: StealCapturedStarshipToLocationEffect recursively assigns new owner to all attached cards, including Effects; executed Special Modifications case confirms the discrepancy.

Generic Alter, shuffle and card actions are top-level actions, not freely usable responses to theft. Explicit pinned just-stolen handlers are device-specific Binders and saber-specific recovery/protection; they do not target the ship in this fixture.
A positive post-theft top-level baseline offers the same in-hand shuffle action that was absent from both STOLEN response menus.
limitations: Controlled initial ship placement, Force activation and prepared destiny6; actual deployments, battle and beam action afterward. No injected capture/theft action and no production source override.
No non-empty theft response was executed. These candidate menus are a bounded negative result, not proof every possible card interaction has empty responses.
Reference snapshot contains ownership-before-placement STOLEN state. Raw data remains unchanged.
Attached Effect ownership is an explicitly retained rules/GEMP disagreement, not conformance.
